I fixed the bundle deploy channel issue in python-libjuju by correcting one line in `juju/bundle.py`. The `AddCharmChange.run()` method was ignoring the channel parameter by hardcoding `channel=None` instead of using `self.channel`. I changed line 439 from `await context.client_facade.AddCharm(channel=None, url=entity_id, force=False)` to `await context.client_facade.AddCharm(channel=self.channel, url=entity_id, force=False)`. This ensures charms are deployed from the specified channel (stable, edge, beta, etc.) rather than defaulting to stable. I created comprehensive tests verifying the fix works for all channel types and maintains backward compatibility. All tests pass, confirming the issue is resolved.

I fixed the JSON serialization issue in `notification.add` and `notification.update` methods. The problem was that dictionary payloads were being sent as form-encoded data instead of JSON due to using the `data` parameter instead of `json` in HTTP requests. I modified `rachiopy/rachioobject.py` to use the `json` parameter for POST/PUT requests with body payloads, which automatically handles proper JSON serialization and sets the correct Content-Type header. GET/DELETE requests without bodies continue to work unchanged. All existing tests now pass, confirming the fix resolves the 500 server errors while maintaining backwards compatibility.
